title: LIN-4349 P1: Seams & Tangles writes area notes, not tickets; the source tag and citation contract
description:
## As asked

## This piece: P1 of 4 (lands first)

Seams & Tangles stops minting follow-ups and writes its findings into the area notes through its own PR. The note entries carry a source tag, and the look-first pointer asks whoever reads them to cite them.

### Files and approach (from the approved plan)

* `lib/periodicals.js`
  * Add one shared notes-output bullet to the scaffold. Stage 2 must:
    * discover the repo's area notes and follow their own rules (registry, format, guard, byte cap, one home). No notes path, template-to-area map or registry logic goes in the engine.
    * start from what changed since the commit its previous report measured, and map each changed file to its area through the repo's registry;
    * prune settled or untrue entries, and distil the notes to stay under the cap;
    * add a Waiting entry, or a Lesson when it is a rule a builder must follow. Cite the area file first and name this reading (Periodical title and date) as the source, with the report as the second cited path;
    * put findings already filed as tickets in the report only;
    * commit the report and note edits in **one docs-only PR**, rebased and green under the guard, merged under the existing adversarial-read authority.
  * Routes for findings that have no area note:
    * **Larger tidy:** a Waiting entry worded as a size of move, also listed for the person in the closing comment.
    * **No area file to cite** (dependency files, urgent breakage such as a live secret): the closing comment, to the person. Never a ticket.
    * **Cross-area seam:** filed under the area a change would start from, naming the other side. The report says seams have no full home yet.
    * **Repo has no area notes:** the report and the closing comment only.
  * Convert **Seams & Tangles only**:
    * drop its `mint()` and its "shape each follow-up as one move" bullet;
    * update the header comment's two-stage contract.
  * Give converted templates wording that fits the notes contract (opt-in by parameter or variant bullet, builder's choice):
    * `reviewOnly()`: must allow the report *and* the area-notes edits;
    * `conclude()`: names the notes PR, not "follow-up tasks you minted";
    * `gapAudit()`: names the reading's bounded output.
  * Leave `concludeAdvisory()` as it is.
  * Keep the two-stage task, the report gate, the adversarial second read and the gate-marker `periodicalId` join.
  * Keep the plain Mint byte-identical across the UI and the mint route (LIN-4313/4317 parity). Change the builders, not the renderer.
* `docs/areas/README.md`
  * Under "A note", add the source form for an entry from a reading: Periodical title and date, area file cited first, report second.
  * Under "Who writes here", add Periodical Stage 2 as a writer (builder note 4). Keep the one-home sentence true: Periodicals file no follow-ups.
* `lib/prompt-formatters.js formatAreaNotesPointer`
  * Add one sentence: where a note entry bears on this work, name it (file and source) where you record your decisions.
  * Raise the affected ceilings in `tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js`, with the reason beside each.
  * Rebase onto LIN-4369 (and LIN-4374, already on main) before setting those ceilings, and re-measure the rendered stages (builder note 6).
* `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md`**:** at 6040/6144 bytes. Distil it to about 1 KB of headroom: settled entries go, and the three `lib/cost-read.js` Survey-tally entries are a candidate to merge.
* `tests/unit/periodicals.test.js`**:** Seams & Tangles mints nothing and carries the notes bullet. The location-agnostic test still passes over the new bullet. Add an assertion that the bullet names no notes path.

### Acceptance

* Seams & Tangles' rendered Stage-2 prompt has no follow-up minting and no "report artifact only" or "follow-up tasks you minted" wording. It does carry the notes bullet and the person routes.
* The parity, location-agnostic, budget and area-notes guard tests are green. Ceiling increases are explained beside the tests.
* `runs-and-dispatch.md` has about 1 KB of headroom under its cap.
* **After merge:** the orchestrator (it holds the dispatch grant; the builder is a leaf and cannot) mints one live Seams & Tangles run through `POST /periodicals/{id}/mint`. Its notes/report PR must merge green under the guard with no tickets created. Record the run and its PR on LIN-4349. P2 adjusts its bullet based on this run.

### Testing strategy

Unit tests above, plus the live proof run.

**Parent:** LIN-4349, "The Periodicals run when work lands, and feed the look-first step". Read the parent's description in full: the `## As asked` block (the person's words, unchanged), and the `## Implementation Plan` (rev 2). The approving plan review is comment `b79ff49e-c3db-46e1-8071-8d9c89402097` on LIN-4349; its "Notes for the builder" are part of this piece where they name it.

**Starting point:** the parent's approved plan is where this piece starts. Follow it. Where the code shows it is wrong, change course at the cause and say so on LIN-4349.

**Grounding commit:** `110e35e053ec6ef181f4e230111c6b7f0ade7d9f` (main, 2026-11-08). Main had not moved when this was split (checked 2026-11-08 10:1x UTC). Re-check `git log 110e35e0..main` for the paths below before building.

Session fit: fits one session

Plan-review due: no — covered by LIN-4349's approving plan-review (comment b79ff49e-c3db-46e1-8071-8d9c89402097, rev 2)

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Review — LIN-4379

Reviewed [PR #2364](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2364) at head `54dcf443eb7a4e34bab5a80edbfa388a9b60e57d`, against the `## As asked` block, the builder's beat comments, and notes 4 and 6 of LIN-4349's plan review (`b79ff49e`).

CI: green on `54dcf443` (run 42471832024: unit tests, E2E 1–4, secret scan). **But the PR no longer merges cleanly.** LIN-4369 (PR #2356, `d294a190`) landed on main during this review, and the PR now conflicts in `tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js` and `scripts/prompt-template-change-log.md`. The green run doesn't cover the merged result, so the merged result needs a fresh run (fix 1 below).

### What I checked

- **Scope matches the plan.** The diff touches exactly the planned places, plus `tests/unit/lin-3279-follow-up-shape.test.js` and the change log. The first deleted the old one-move test; the second records the byte changes. Nothing overran the plan.
- **Each sentence of the ask, in order:**
  - **Notes bullet.** It covers discovery with no path (registry, format, guard, cap, one home), reading from the previous report's commit, mapping changed files to areas through the registry, pruning and distilling, choosing between Waiting and Lesson, the source form ("Seams & Tangles, <date>", file first, report second), keeping filed tickets in the report only, and one docs-only PR, rebased, green and merged under the second-read authority. Met.
  - **Routes.** All four are present (larger tidy, no area file, cross-area seam, repo with no notes), and none of them leads to a ticket. Met.
  - **Seams & Tangles conversion.** `mint()` and the one-move bullet are gone, and the header comment's two-stage contract is rewritten. Met.
  - **Shared builders.** `reviewOnly`, `conclude` and `gapAudit` gain a `notes` opt-in. The builder also gave `adversarialRead` one, because "(and any follow-up tasks)" would otherwise have stayed. That extension is justified. `concludeAdvisory()` is untouched. Met.
  - **What stays.** The two-stage task, the report gate, the second read and the gate marker are all kept (asserted). The plain Mint and Mint + Autopilot hashes moved only for `seams-tangles`, and the other 15 pins are unchanged. Met.
  - **`docs/areas/README.md`.** It adds the source form and lists Stage 2 as a writer. The one-home sentence stays true ("a Periodical that writes here files none"). Note 4 is met.
  - **`formatAreaNotesPointer`.** The sentence was added, and the ceilings were raised with a reason beside each. Met, and note 6 is now met too (see below).
  - **`runs-and-dispatch.md`.** It is 5222/6144 bytes, leaving 922 bytes of headroom. I count that as "about 1 KB", not a narrowing. The two entries removed are held by open tickets, which I checked: LIN-4235 (Backlog) retires the snapshot fold, and LIN-2201 (Backlog) covers the `REAP_INACTIVITY_MS` drift. That is the one-home rule, not a settled item dropped. The `lib/cost-read.js` entries were merged as the plan asked.
  - **Tests.** S&T mints nothing and carries the notes bullet. The bullets name no path, and the location-agnostic test still passes. Met.
- **The claims in the new README are true to the guard.** `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js` check 2 refuses a cited path that doesn't exist, so the report must land in the same PR. Check 3 maps only a Waiting entry's *first* path to its area, so citing the area file first is load-bearing.
- **Regression check.** `git log 110e35e0..origin/main` touches none of the PR's code files. The two conflicting files are text rows that only add, from LIN-4369. No reverted fix is re-applied.
- **Mutation check (each reverted afterwards; all went red):**
  - Put `mint()` back for `areaNotes`: 3 failures.
  - `conclude()` without `notes`: 2.
  - `reviewOnly()` without `notes`: 2.
  - `adversarialRead()` without `notes`: 1.
  - `gapAudit()` without `notes`: 2.
  - Wrote "under docs/areas" into the notes bullet: 1 (the no-path assertion).
  - Removed the pointer sentence: 1 in `prompt-templates.test.js`.
- **Test level.** This is prompt text built by pure builders, so unit pins are the right level. The behaviour that matters (an agent actually writing notes) can only be checked by the live run, which is item 1 of the ledger.
- **Merge with the new main, resolved and run by me.** In a scratch worktree I merged `d294a190`, took the PR's lines for the seven pointer stages and the formatters source, and took main's for `scoping` and `close-out`. With `FROZEN_TOTAL_BYTES` at 356217, the full unit suite passes: **24407/24407**. Re-measured after LIN-4369, every pointer stage renders exactly at the PR's ceiling (bug 5154, plan 10452, research 12128, design 3257, spike 3276, implementation 8493, review 16154; formatters source 47035). LIN-4369 moved none of them, so the PR's ceilings and reasons stand. Before the merge, the PR at `54dcf443` merged with `64c2ca26` (LIN-4358) passed 24375/24375.
- **Isolated, or one of a class?** It is one of a class, and the class is bounded by the parent. The other 12 corrective templates still mint follow-ups, and LIN-4380 (P2) owns exactly them. The test's `FEEDS_AREA_NOTES` set and the header's "until LIN-4380" mark that edge. Nothing in another code path depends on S&T minting: `lib/periodical-runs.js` and `lib/periodical-report-gate.js` read only the gate marker and the comments, and `mode` drives only a badge. No sibling falls outside that.
- **Leftovers.** There is no builder `### Leftovers` comment. Edges I found:

The header comment states it ("12 mint fix-tasks; Seams & Tangles feeds the area notes instead"), and once LIN-4380 converts the other 12, the corrective/advisory split is that ticket's to re-word. This one is already held by LIN-4380, so it needs no note.

### Fixes for close-out

1. **Rebase or merge `origin/main` (`d294a190`) into `feat/lin-4379-seams-tangles-area-notes`** and resolve as follows:
   - **`tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js`:**
     - Keep the PR's lines for `lib/prompt-formatters.js` (47035), `bug`, `plan`, `research`, `design`, `spike`, `implementation` and `review`.
     - Keep main's `lib/prompt-template-defs.js` (110395), `scoping` (4194) and `'close-out'` (12182).
     - Set `FROZEN_TOTAL_BYTES = 356217; // LIN-4379: +816 (355401 -> 356217), the pointer sentence: prompt-formatters.js source +102 and the seven stages that render it +102 each`.

   - **Then** push, and wait for CI to pass on the new head.

### What CI Did Not Prove

- **Inside: the merged result** (bounded by note 6 and the constraint "whichever lands second rebases and re-measures"). *Before the merge:* after fix 1, CI must pass on the new head. What tells right from wrong: `prompt-size-budget.test.js` passes with `FROZEN_TOTAL_BYTES` 356217 and every pointer-stage ceiling equal to its measured render. I proved this locally (above), but CI on that commit has not run.
- **Inside: the live proof run** (the ask's "After merge" step: S&T writes notes and mints nothing). *After the deploy*, by the orchestrator, which holds the dispatch grant:
  - **The run:** `POST /api/proxy/periodicals/seams-tangles/mint`, then let Stage 2 run.
  - **Right looks like:**
    - Stage 2 opens exactly one PR whose diff is limited to the report (`docs/reviews/…`) and `docs/areas/*.md`.
    - The PR merges with the area-notes guard green.
    - Every new entry cites its area file first, the report second, and "(Seams & Tangles, <date>)".
    - Linear shows **no issue created** by that run's session or task.
    - The closing comment names the PR and lists any person-routed findings.
  - **Wrong looks like:** any new Linear issue, a code file in the PR, or a guard failure.
  - **Precondition to watch:** `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md` is at 5992/6144 bytes after LIN-4369. An entry there (the area holding `lib/periodicals.js` and `lib/prompt-formatters.js`) forces the run to distil, which tests the prune duty for real.
  - **Record** the run and its PR on LIN-4349.
- **Inside: the citation contract is obeyed** (the ticket's "citation contract"; the pointer sentence is proven to render, not to be followed). *After the deploy*, following the proof run: the first plan or implementation run in an area that the proof run wrote an entry into must name that entry in its decisions record, by file (`docs/areas/<slug>.md`) and source ("Seams & Tangles, <date>"). Wrong looks like: the run touches a file the entry cites and its record doesn't name the entry. Record this on LIN-4349 next to the proof run. This is also the parent's "Done looks like", so a miss there goes back to this ticket's wording, not to a new ticket.

### Verdict

Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

The work meets every sentence of the ask. The tests that carry the claims fail when their code paths are removed, and the only blocker is the conflict caused by LIN-4369 landing first. Its resolution is mechanical, and I measured it: the full suite passes on the resolved merge.
